## DslTestRunner

```csharp
public sealed class DslTestRunner
```

Runs `test` blocks. Each test gets a fresh runtime with a player (80 hp, 3 energy) and seed 1. Setup statements run first; the battle starts, without shuffling or drawing, at the first statement that is not setup.

**Example.** ```
test "Fireball kills a 6 HP enemy"
  setup: enemy hp 6
  play Fireball on enemy
  expect enemy.dead
```

### Constructors

```csharp
public DslTestRunner(ContentLibrary content)
```

*Undocumented.*

### Properties

```csharp
public Action<CardRuntime>? ConfigureRuntime { get; set; }
```

Runs on each test's new runtime before the test's first line, for the verbs the game registers in C#: `runner.ConfigureRuntime = runtime => runtime.RegisterVerb("corrupt", Corrupt);`. The runtime has no player yet. If this creates one, the test uses it; otherwise the test creates one with 80 hp and 3 energy. The test verbs are registered afterwards, so they win over a verb of the same name. `play` is the exception, because it is a rule verb too: the test's wins only for the `play` statements in the test's own body, and every other one goes to whatever was registered before — the rules', or the game's. An exception from this fails that test.

```csharp
public Func<IEffectHost>? CreateHost { get; set; }
```

Makes the host for each test's runtime, for content that uses names or functions the game answers in C#: `runner.CreateHost = () => new GameHost();`. It is called once per test, so each test starts with a host of its own. Null, the default, gives each test a host that adds nothing.

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyCollection<string> TestVerbs { get; }
```

Verbs that only exist inside `test` blocks.

```csharp
public bool Trace { get; set; }
```

Record the causality trace for every test (slower; attached to failures). The trace also holds what `log` statements wrote, which a test otherwise shows nowhere.
